column1: Water Quality Data from PISCES 2 located at the Slave River at Fitzgerald
Data File Name
Date File Generated
Context Note
column2:
In 2012, Environment Canada installed and operated a new automated monitoring platform on the Slave River at Fitzgerald, Alberta (JOSM site M11a). The objective is to provide near real-time, continuous water quality data to expand on regular monitoring done by conventional “grab samples” at this and other sites on the Athabasca River.
Verified and validated water quality data from the summer and fall of 2012 (June through September) collected at the Slave River at Fitzgerald site (M11a) is being released. Measurements are reported for water temperature, turbidity, dissolved oxygen, pH, and specific conductance at 1m and 4 m depths every two hours. Weather observations (air temperature, wind speed and direction, barometric pressure, precipitation and relative humidity) are collected every 15 minutes.
Analysis of the data being released is still ongoing. As of the time of this data release, the time series of data is too limited to draw any conclusions. As the data increases with continued monitoring, it will provide an indication of water quality at the northern end of the oil sands region before water flows into Lake Athabasca. In future, the water quality data from the automated platform, along with other environmental measures, will be used to assess the spatial and temporal status and trends in water quality in the mainstem of the Athabasca, Peace and Slave rivers.
The automated monitoring platform is an EMM350 PISCES (Pontoon for In-Situ Characterization of Environmental Systems - see Figure 1). PISCES consists of data acquisition components including a YSI 6600 water quality multi-probe, satellite communication capabilities, and an on-board power management system using solar panels.
